articles.title: Longtime host Michael Wilbon steps away from ESPN due to ‘health issues’
articles.summary: Pardon the Interruption co-host to take leave of absence. Wilbon did not go into detail but cited ‘worrisome signs’ Michael Wilbon, the co-host of ESPN’s popular Pardon the Interruption talkshow alongside good friend Tony Kornheiser announced on Monday he is taking a leave of absence because of…
body: Wilbon, who turns 68 later this month, wrote in a post on X that he is taking a trip to “the injured list” but added he hopes it is “not an extended one”.

While Wilbon, who is also featured on ESPN’s NBA coverage, declined to go into detail about his situation, he added that there are people in his personal life who noticed “worrisome signs” in recent years that he largely ignored. Wilbon did make a point to note the issues are not alcohol or gambling-related.
“I have no idea how exactly this part of my journey will wind up,” Wilbon posted. “The goal is to come out of it feeling much better than I do now and ready to return to sparring with Tony.”
Wilbon’s last appearance on PTI, which recently celebrated its 25th anniversary and is credited with revolutionizing television’s “sports debate” format, was on 26 October.

articles.title: Fifa to share confidential World Cup sell-off plan documents
articles.summary: Fifa has informed members of its Council that they will be granted access to view some documents related to president Gianni Infantino's failed plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
body: Last month, Uefa gave football's world governing body until 2 November to release details about the hugely controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, and to answer a list of questions relating to its governance and decision-making.

That followed a council meeting at which Infantino apologised for the abandoned sell-off plot but failed to offer a full explanation for how the proposal was devised, asking that questions be submitted in writing.

Just hours before the deadline from European football's governing body passed, Fifa secretary general Mattias Grafstrom wrote to members of its main decision-making body - saying they will be able to view "key documents", but only in person at the organisation's headquarters in Zurich.

In his letter - seen by BBC Sport - he says the paperwork will be available "under strict review protocols to preserve confidentiality", with council members asked to register to see them within the next two weeks.

articles.title: Alex Mitchell out of Nations Championship opener in fresh England injury blow
articles.summary: Scrum-half out of game against Australia on Sunday. Wallabies match followed by New Zealand and Japan. The Northampton scrum-half Alex Mitchell has been ruled out of England’s November opener against Australia on Sunday, with Bristol’s Harry Randall and Bath’s Ben Spencer called into the squad…
body: Mitchell, established as the first‑choice No 9 under Borthwick, damaged a hamstring in Northampton’s Prem win against Gloucester on Saturday and will have a scan on Tuesday to determine the extent of the injury.

Archie McParland, Mitchell’s uncapped clubmate, is also sidelined for the Wallabies match after sustaining a calf injury training with England last week, following his second call-up to the senior squad. A major scrum-half rethink is consequently needed by Borthwick before a highly significant sequence of four Nations Championship matches.
The injury-enforced absence of Mitchell and McParland means either Randall or Spencer will be on the bench against Australia, with Leicester’s Jack van Poortvliet expected to start at No 9.

While Mitchell is guaranteed to return when he recovers from injury, this week represents a priceless chance for Randall and Spencer to state their respective cases, with the World Cup less than a year away.

articles.title: Stumbling block: Wirtz's and Liverpool’s costly struggles against tight defences | Andrew Beasley
articles.summary: Credit to Arsenal for restricting opportunities at Anfield but Iraola will need his side to learn to unpick low backlines. Liverpool did not have a shot on target in their 1-0 defeat by Arsenal on Sunday, according to Opta, the first time they have drawn this type of blank in a Premier League game…
body: If Alexis Mac Allister’s floated ball from distance into David Raya’s waiting arms had actually counted as a shot, would Andoni Iraola’s side have delivered a markedly better attacking performance? Far more concerning for the Spaniard will be that his team had 52 touches in the Arsenal penalty area (which is good) to create only one Opta‑defined big chance (which is bad). The Premier League average this season is five times more efficient; 10.3 box touches per big chance.

Credit to Arsenal for restricting the quality of Liverpool’s chances despite them getting repeatedly within range of their goal. Most teams have been able to do this, though. While 12 teams have had fewer touches in opposition penalty boxes than Liverpool, only Coventry with 11 have generated fewer big chances this season than Liverpool’s 12. Everton’s Thierno Barry alone has had 15, while Manchester City’s Erling Haaland has also had more than Liverpool with 14.

articles.title: Australia's Maxwell announces retirement from international cricket
articles.summary: Australia all-rounder Glenn Maxwell has announced his retirement from international cricket but will continue to play T20 for Melbourne Stars in the Big Bash League.
body: The 38-year-old's final appearance for his country came against Oman in the T20 World Cup earlier this year, when he recorded figures of 2-13 from three overs with his off-spin and was not required to bat.

Maxwell scored five T20 international hundreds, a record he shares with India's Rohit Sharma, while he is one of only five Australian men, alongside Shane Watson, David Warner, Josh Inglis and Mitchell Marsh, to score a ton in all three international formats.

Speaking on the Final Word podcast, Maxwell said: "I suppose [I had] a small hope that I might have been able to potentially get a send-off game at the MCG. But I can completely understand the direction they're going with this [T20] squad.

"There's going to be a lot of change over the next 12 to 24 months with the Olympics coming up [in 2028], and they've got to make sure they get their eyeballs on a few young guys coming through, making sure they're getting exposed to international pressure."

articles.title: Tenerife player in intensive care with injury
articles.summary: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel is in a stable condition in intensive care after suffering a serious injury during a Spanish second division match on Monday.
body: The 30-year-old suffered injuries in the region of his head and chest in added time of Tenerife's home fixture against Andorra, following a collision with visiting goalkeeper Jesus Owono.
Spanish media, including Marca, external, reported De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest in the ambulance and was resuscitated by paramedics on the way to hospital.
A statement from Tenerife said the Madrid-born De Miguel was admitted to the University Hospital of Nuestra Senora de Candelaria and was "stable despite the severity of his condition".
Tenerife and Andorra were tied 2-2 and seven minutes into stoppage time when the incident occurred.

articles.title: Smyth in contention as Saints evaluate kicker slot
articles.summary: Head coach Kellen Moore says the New Orleans Saints will "evaluate" kickers Dan Carlson and Charlie Smyth ahead of Sunday's game with the Cleveland Browns.
body: Carlson has been the Saints' first-choice kicker this season, but the 31-year-old has struggled for consistency.

Smyth, a former Gaelic footballer from Mayobridge in County Down, made his NFL debut last season but returned to the practice roster after the Saints elected to bring in Carlson for the start of the current campaign.

However, Carlson's form has opened the door for Smyth to potentially return to the playing roster. Moore said both he and his coaching staff will "evaluate the field goal situation and opportunities".
Moore said that the Saints had not brought any additional kickers into their squad, which leaves Smyth and Carlson in contention to start against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday.

articles.title: Edwards: Borthwick turned down my offer to work with England
articles.summary: Renowned defence coach Shaun Edwards says England boss Steve Borthwick turned down his offer to work with the side at the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia.
body: Edwards ended a six-year spell with France - during which Les Bleus won three Six Nations, including back-to-back in 2025 and 2026 - earlier this year.
The 60-year-old worked with the England women's team on a short-term basis and has now moved onto Argentina's staff until the end of next year's World Cup, which runs across October and November.

Speaking to the BBC's Rugby Union Weekly podcast, Edwards said: "I had a good chat with Steve [Borthwick] over the phone. I said he can make me assistant kit man and I'll be there, I'll be ready for work.
"He was very, very honest with me and I thanked him for that. He said he was happy with his staff and the way things have been going, and I respected him for that."

articles.title: Who Will Replace FSU's Mike Norvell? 5 Coaching Candidates To Watch
articles.summary: As the college football coaching carousel continues to grow, Florida State made its move after firing Mike Norvell following its 36-24 loss to Clemson. Offensive analyst Rick Stockstill has been named interim head coach for the remainder of the season.
body: Florida State has yet to clinch a double-digit win season since 2023, when it finished 11-3. So who should the program target as it begins its head coaching search?

Georgia defensive coordinator and linebackers coach Glenn Schumann could be one of the coordinators to watch in this coaching carousel. Especially as Schumann leads a defense that sits atop the SEC in points allowed per game with 14.1, he would bring the defensive leadership that Florida State could be looking for if it wants to climb towards ACC dominance. This season under Norvell, Florida State ranked 127th in total defense and allowed an average of 427 yards per game.

New Mexico’s Jason Eck has emerged as a name to watch in this season's carousel. Although he’s a head coach with offensive line experience, Eck has led the Lobos to an impressive 7-1 start, with their only loss to then-No. 14 Oklahoma. In his second season as New Mexico’s coach, Eck has proven to be a winner, compiling an overall 16-5 record and a 10-2 conference record. After seven seasons with Norvell, Florida State could benefit from an up-and-coming coach with only five losses on his résumé.
